sentences.zh: ○苗晉卿裴冕裴遵慶子向向子寅寅子樞=苗晉卿=苗晉卿，上黨壺關人。

translations.literal: ○ Miao Jinqing, Pei Mian, Pei Zunqing, son Xiang, grandson Yin, great-grandson Shu = Miao Jinqing = Miao Jinqing, a native of Huguan in Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: [Biographies:] Miao Jinqing; Pei Mian; Pei Zunqing (and descendants Xiang, Yin, and Shu). — Miao Jinqing was a native of Huguan in Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 世以儒素稱。

translations.literal: For generations his family was praised for Confucian learning and plain integrity.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the family was known for scholarly refinement and unadorned virtue.

sentences.zh: 祖夔，高道不仕，追贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: His grandfather Kui, of lofty virtue and did not take office, was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Kui, a man of lofty principle who never entered official service, was posthumously granted the title Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 父殆庶，官至絳州龍門縣丞，早卒，以晉卿贈太子少保。

translations.literal: His father Dai Shu reached the post of Assistant Magistrate of Longmen in Jiang Prefecture, died early, and because of Jinqing was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dai Shu had risen to assistant magistrate of Longmen in Jiang Prefecture but died young; on account of Jinqing he was later posthumously honored as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 晉卿幼好學，善屬文，進士擢第。

translations.literal: Jinqing from youth loved learning, was skilled at literary composition, and passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Jinqing loved study and wrote well; he eventually passed the jinshi civil examination.

sentences.zh: 初授懷州修武縣尉，歷奉先縣尉，坐累貶徐州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed magistrate of Xiuwu in Huai Prefecture, served as magistrate of Fengxian, and because of implicated guilt was demoted to Registrar of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was first appointed magistrate of Xiuwu in Huai Prefecture, later served at Fengxian, and was then demoted to registrar in Xuzhou after being implicated in a case.

sentences.zh: 秩滿隨調，判入高等，授萬年縣尉。

translations.literal: When his term ended he followed the regular reassignment; his examination essay was graded in the highest class, and he was appointed magistrate of Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired he entered the regular reassignment cycle; his evaluation placed him in the top tier, and he received appointment as magistrate of Wannian.

sentences.zh: 遷侍御史，歷度支、兵、吏部三員外郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attending Censor and successively served as Vice Director in the Ministries of Revenue, War, and Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Attending Censor and in turn held vice-director posts in the ministries of Revenue, War, and Personnel.

sentences.zh: 開元二十三年，遷吏部郎中。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan he was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan year 23 he was made a director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，與吏部郎中孫逖並拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he and Sun Ti, Director in the Ministry of Personnel, were together appointed Drafting Attendants at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he and Sun Ti of the Ministry of Personnel were jointly appointed drafting attendants at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，以本官權知吏部選事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, in his existing post he was given provisional charge of personnel selection in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In year 27 he was placed in provisional charge of civil-service selection while retaining his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 晉卿性謙柔，選人有訴訟索好官者，雖至數千言，或聲色甚厲者，晉卿必含容之，略無慍色。

translations.literal: Jinqing's nature was modest and gentle; when candidates came to plead lawsuits seeking good posts, even if they spoke thousands of words or their voice and manner were very fierce, Jinqing always bore with them and showed not the slightest anger.
translations.idiomatic: Jinqing was by nature modest and forbearing. Candidates who came to argue their cases and demand better appointments might harangue him for thousands of words or raise their voices in fury, yet he always received them patiently and never showed irritation.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，拜吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In year 29 he was appointed vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 前後典選五年，政既寬弛，胥吏多因緣為奸，賄賂大行。

translations.literal: Before and after he presided over selection for five years; administration was already lax, clerks often used opportunities to commit wrongdoing, and bribery flourished greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Over five years in charge of selection his administration grew lax; clerks seized every opening for corruption, and bribery became rampant.

sentences.zh: 時天下承平，每年赴選常萬余人。

translations.literal: At that time the realm enjoyed peace, and each year those coming for selection commonly exceeded ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was at peace, and each year more than ten thousand candidates presented themselves for examination.

sentences.zh: 李林甫為尚書，專任廟堂，銓事唯委晉卿及同列侍郎宋遙主之。

translations.literal: Li Linfu was Minister and monopolized court affairs; selection matters were entrusted only to Jinqing and his fellow Vice Minister Song Yao to manage.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu held the ministry post and dominated the court; he left selection affairs entirely to Jinqing and his colleague Song Yao.

sentences.zh: 選人既多，每年兼命他官有識者同考定書判，務求其實。

translations.literal: Because candidates were numerous, each year they also ordered other officials of discernment jointly to examine and grade the written judgments, striving for truth.
translations.idiomatic: With so many candidates, each year additional officials of judgment were assigned to grade the examination essays together, in an effort to keep the process honest.

sentences.zh: 天寶二年春，御史中丞張倚男奭參選，晉卿與遙以倚初承恩，欲悅附之，考選人判等凡六十四人，分甲乙丙科，奭在其首。

translations.literal: In spring of the second year of Tianbao, Censor-in-Chief Zhang Yi's son Shi entered selection; Jinqing and Yao, because Zhang Yi had newly received favor, wished to please and attach themselves to him; they examined candidates' judgment grades totaling sixty-four persons, divided into jia, yi, and bing classes, with Shi at the head.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Tianbao 2, Censor-in-Chief Zhang Yi's son Shi sat for the examinations. Jinqing and Yao, wishing to curry favor with the newly favored Zhang Yi, ranked sixty-four candidates in three tiers—and placed Shi at the top.

sentences.zh: 眾知奭不讀書，論議紛然。

translations.literal: The multitude knew Shi did not read books, and discussion became clamorous.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone knew Shi was illiterate, and public outcry followed.

sentences.zh: 有蘇孝慍者，嘗為范陽薊令，事安祿山，具其事告之。

translations.literal: There was one Su Xiaoyin who had once been magistrate of Ji in Fanyang, served An Lushan, and reported the whole affair in detail.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Su Xiaoyin, formerly magistrate of Ji in Fanyang and now in An Lushan's service, reported the affair in full.

sentences.zh: 祿山恩寵特異，謁見不常，因而奏之。

translations.literal: Lushan enjoyed exceptional favor and was not often granted audience, so he reported it through that channel.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan enjoyed extraordinary favor and was rarely granted audience at court, so the matter reached the emperor by that route.

sentences.zh: 玄宗大集登科人，禦花萼樓親試，登第者十無一二；

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong greatly gathered those who had passed the examinations, personally tested them at the Hua'e Tower, and of those who had passed the examination scarcely one or two in ten;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong summoned all recent degree-holders to the Hua'e Tower for a personal examination; scarcely one candidate in ten could truly pass;

sentences.zh: 而奭手持試紙，竟日不下一字，時謂之「曳白」。

translations.literal: but Shi held the examination paper and for a whole day did not write a single character; at the time they called this 'dragging blank paper.'
translations.idiomatic: Shi, holding his examination paper, could not write a single character all day—the scandal was dubbed 'dragging a blank sheet.'

sentences.zh: 上怒，晉卿貶為安康郡太守，遙為武當郡太守，張倚為淮陽太守。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry; Jinqing was demoted to Prefect of Ankang Commandery, Yao to Prefect of Wudang Commandery, and Zhang Yi to Prefect of Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious. Jinqing was demoted to prefect of Ankang, Yao to prefect of Wudang, and Zhang Yi to prefect of Huaiyang.

sentences.zh: 敕曰：「門庭之間，不能訓子；

translations.literal: An edict said: 'Within one's own household one cannot instruct one's son;
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: 'You cannot discipline your own son within your own household;

sentences.zh: 選調之際，仍以托人。

translations.literal: at the time of selection and assignment one still relies on pulling strings for others.'
translations.idiomatic: yet at selection time you still pull strings for others.'

sentences.zh: 」時士子皆以為戲笑。

translations.literal: ' At the time scholars all took it as a jest.
translations.idiomatic: ' Scholars everywhere treated the edict as a public joke.

sentences.zh: 天寶三載閏二月，轉魏郡太守，充河北采訪處置使，居職三年，政化洽聞。

translations.literal: In the intercalary second month of the third year of Tianbao he was transferred to Prefect of Wei Commandery and appointed Hebei Investigation and Disposition Commissioner; in office three years, his governance and transforming influence were widely heard.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary second month of Tianbao 3 he became prefect of Wei and Hebei investigation commissioner; after three years in post his benevolent rule was renowned throughout the region.

sentences.zh: 會入計，因上表請歸鄉里。

translations.literal: When he came to the capital for the annual accounting he submitted a memorial requesting to return to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: When he traveled to the capital for the annual review he memorialized the throne asking leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 既至壺關，望縣門而步。

translations.literal: When he reached Huguan he saw the county gate and walked on foot.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Huguan he dismounted and walked on foot as he approached the county gate.

sentences.zh: 小吏進曰：「太守位高德重，不宜自輕。

translations.literal: A petty clerk came forward and said: 'The prefect's position is high and his virtue weighty; he should not belittle himself.
translations.idiomatic: A clerk stepped forward and said, 'Your post is exalted and your standing great—you should not humble yourself in this way.

sentences.zh: 」晉卿曰：「《禮》：『下公門，式路馬。

translations.literal: ' Jinqing said: 'The Rites says: "When descending from the duke's gate, stroke the roadside horses."
translations.idiomatic: ' Jinqing replied, 'The Rites of Zhou says that when one passes the duke's gate one must bow to the horses tied along the road.

sentences.zh: 』況父母之邦，所宜尊敬。

translations.literal: ' How much more is one's parents' homeland what one ought to revere.
translations.idiomatic: ' How much more should one show respect in the land of one's parents!

sentences.zh: 汝何言哉！

translations.literal: What words are you speaking!
translations.idiomatic: What sort of talk is that!

sentences.zh: 」大會鄉黨，歡飲累日而去。

translations.literal: ' He held a great gathering of the township and kin, drank in joy for many days, and then departed.
translations.idiomatic: ' He then feasted the township for days before taking his leave.

sentences.zh: 又俸錢三萬為鄉學本，以教授子弟。

translations.literal: He also set aside thirty thousand in salary cash as capital for the district school, to instruct the young clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: He also endowed the local school with thirty thousand cash from his salary to educate the village youth.

sentences.zh: 尋改河東太守、河東采訪使，入為尚書、東京留守，征為憲部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to Prefect of Hedong and Hedong Investigation Commissioner, entered the capital as Minister and Eastern Capital Regent, and was summoned as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Hedong as prefect and investigation commissioner, then recalled to serve as a ministry director and regent of the Eastern Capital before being summoned as minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 屬祿山叛逆，楊國忠以晉卿有時望，將抑之，乃奏云：「宜以大臣鎮東道。

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled, Yang Guozhong, because Jinqing had contemporary renown and wished to suppress him, memorialized saying: 'A great minister ought to guard the eastern circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan rose in rebellion, Yang Guozhong—fearing Jinqing's public prestige and wishing to sideline him—memorialized that a senior minister should be posted to guard the eastern circuits.

sentences.zh: 」遂出為陜州刺史、陜虢兩州防禦使。

translations.literal: ' He was then sent out as Prefect of Shan Prefecture and Defense Commissioner of the two prefectures Shan and Guo.
translations.idiomatic: ' Jinqing was accordingly sent out as prefect of Shan and defense commissioner for Shan and Guo.

sentences.zh: 及入對，固辭老病，由是忤旨，改憲部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: When he entered for audience he firmly declined on grounds of age and illness; thereby he offended the imperial will and was changed to Minister of Justice with retirement.
translations.idiomatic: At his audience he firmly pleaded age and illness; this displeased the emperor, and he was reassigned as retired minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 及朝廷失守，衣冠流離道路，多為逆黨所脅，自陳希烈、張均已下數十人盡赴洛陽，晉卿潛遁山谷，南投金州。

translations.literal: When the court lost the capital, officials in caps and robes wandered the roads, many compelled by the rebel party; from Chen Xilie and Zhang Jun down, several tens all went to Luoyang; Jinqing secretly fled into mountain valleys and went south to Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, officials fled along the roads, many forced into rebel service. Dozens from Chen Xilie and Zhang Jun down surrendered to Luoyang; Jinqing slipped into the hills and made his way south to Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會肅宗至鳳翔，手詔追晉卿赴行在，即日拜為左相，軍國大務悉以咨之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong reached Fengxiang, by handwritten edict he summoned Jinqing to the mobile court; that same day he was appointed Left Chancellor, and all great affairs of army and state were entirely entrusted to his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong reached Fengxiang he issued a personal edict recalling Jinqing to the mobile court and that same day named him left chancellor, consulting him on every major military and civil matter.

sentences.zh: 既收兩京，以功封韓國公，食實封五百戶，改為侍中。

translations.literal: After recovering the two capitals, for merit he was enfeoffed Duke of Han with five hundred households of substantive fief, and changed to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After the two capitals were retaken he was enfeoffed as Duke of Han with a substantive fief of five hundred households and appointed palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 後以賊寇漸除，屢乞骸骨，優詔許之，罷知政事，為太子太傅。

translations.literal: Later, because bandits were gradually eliminated, he repeatedly begged to surrender his bones; a gracious edict permitted it, he ceased managing state affairs, and became Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: As the rebels were gradually suppressed he repeatedly asked to retire; the emperor graciously agreed, relieved him of administrative duties, and made him grand tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝思舊臣，復拜為侍中。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor thought of old ministers and again appointed him Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the emperor, remembering his old minister, again appointed him palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 晉卿寬厚廉謹，為政舉大綱，不問小過，所到有惠化。

translations.literal: Jinqing was generous, honest, and cautious; in governing he grasped the great outline and did not inquire into small faults; wherever he went there was benevolent transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Jinqing was magnanimous, upright, and cautious in office. He governed by broad principles, overlooked petty faults, and left benevolent traces wherever he served.

sentences.zh: 魏人思之，為立碑頌德。

translations.literal: The people of Wei remembered him and erected a stele praising his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wei cherished his memory and raised a stele in praise of his virtue.

sentences.zh: 及秉鈞衡，小心畏慎，未嘗忤人意。

translations.literal: When he held the balance of state he was careful and fearful in caution and never once went against people's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held the scales of state power he remained circumspect and never gave offense.

sentences.zh: 性聰敏，達練事體，百司文簿，經目必曉，而修身守位，以智自全，議者比漢之胡廣。

translations.literal: By nature intelligent and quick, skilled and practiced in the substance of affairs, the documents of the hundred offices—once he passed his eyes over them he always understood; yet he cultivated himself and guarded his position, preserving himself by wisdom; commentators compared him to Hu Guang of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted and thoroughly versed in affairs, he could grasp any document from the hundred offices at a glance; yet he cultivated himself and guarded his post, preserving himself through tact—commentators compared him to Hu Guang of the Han.

sentences.zh: 玄宗崩，肅宗詔晉卿攝冢宰。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong died, Emperor Suzong ordered Jinqing to act as regent chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong died, Suzong ordered Jinqing to serve as acting regent.

sentences.zh: 上表固辭曰：「臣聞古者殷高宗在諒闇之中，百官聽於冢宰，更無事跡，但存文字。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial firmly declining, saying: 'Your servant has heard that in antiquity, when King Gaozong of Yin was in the dark of mourning, the hundred officials listened to the regent chancellor—there are no further traces of affairs, only written words remain.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized a firm refusal: 'I have read that in antiquity, when King Gaozong of Yin mourned in seclusion, the hundred officials took orders from the regent—but we have only textual records of that precedent, not living practice.

sentences.zh: 且一時之事，禮不相沿。

translations.literal: Moreover it was a matter of one time; rites do not follow in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover that was a unique moment in history; ritual precedent does not carry forward unchanged.

sentences.zh: 今殘寇猶虞，日殷萬務，皆緣兵馬屯守討襲，善算良謀，立勝擒敵。

translations.literal: Now remnant rebels still cause concern; daily the myriad affairs press urgently—all depend on armies encamped and garrisoned for pursuit and attack, good calculation and fine stratagems, establishing victory and capturing the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Today remnant rebels still threaten the realm and affairs press upon us daily—all depend on armies in the field, sound strategy, and swift victory over the enemy.

sentences.zh: 陛下若行古之道，居喪不言，蒼生何依，百事皆廢。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty follows the ancient way, dwelling in mourning without speaking, on what will the common people rely? A hundred affairs will all be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty followed the ancient way and observed mourning in silence, what would become of the people? Every affair of state would halt.

sentences.zh: 伏讀國家起居註，亦於禮部檢見舊敕，恭惟太宗、高宗、、大行皇帝在位之日，皆有國哀，視事不輟，以為君臨天下，難徇常情。

translations.literal: Your servant has reverently read the national diary of attendance and also in the Ministry of Rites examined old edicts; respectfully considering that during the days in office of Taizong, Gaozong, and the late emperor, whenever there was national mourning they did not cease handling affairs, taking it that to rule all under Heaven one cannot follow ordinary sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: I have studied the court diaries and old edicts in the Ministry of Rites and find that Emperors Taizong and Gaozong, and the late emperor, all continued to conduct state business during periods of national mourning—ruling the realm cannot bow to ordinary private feeling.

sentences.zh: 今遺詔有處分，皇帝宜三日而聽政。

translations.literal: Now the testamentary edict has provisions: the emperor ought on the third day to hear government.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor's testament directs that the new emperor should assume governance after three days.

sentences.zh: 陛下遵太宗故事，則無冢宰；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty follows Taizong's precedent, then there is no regent chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty follows Taizong's precedent, no regent is needed;

sentences.zh: 遵大行皇帝遺詔，便合聽朝。

translations.literal: if Your Majesty follows the late emperor's testamentary edict, then it is fitting to hear court immediately.
translations.idiomatic: if Your Majesty follows the late emperor's testament, you should take the throne at once.

sentences.zh: 萬姓颙颙，不勝大願。

translations.literal: The myriad people look up in hope and cannot bear their great wish.
translations.idiomatic: The people look to you with eager hope beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下知理國之重，順人心之切，以義斷恩，從宜無改。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully considers that Your Majesty knows the weight of governing the state, complies with the urgency of people's hearts, cuts off private feeling by righteousness, and follows what is fitting without change.
translations.idiomatic: I trust Your Majesty understands the weight of governing the realm, the urgency of the people's need, and will set duty above private grief and act as circumstances require.

sentences.zh: 今朝臣一命已上，皆言臣心昏貌朽，加以疾病，事有急速，斷在須臾，凡聖不同，豈合受詔。

translations.literal: Now court ministers of the first rank and above all say your servant's mind is dim and his appearance decayed, moreover afflicted with illness; affairs have urgent speed, decisions must be made in an instant; ordinary and sage are not the same—how could one fittingly receive the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Every minister of the first rank and above says my mind is clouded, my body worn out, and my illnesses many; affairs demand instant decisions—how could a mere mortal accept such a mandate?

sentences.zh: 陛下發哀已五日矣，願準遺詔聽政，則四夷萬國，無任悲幸。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has begun mourning for five days already; I wish you to follow the testament and hear government—then the four barbarians and ten thousand states will be unable to bear their grief and joy.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has mourned five days already; I beg you to follow the testament and resume governance—the four quarters and all nations would be overwhelmed with grief and joy.

sentences.zh: 」肅宗時疾彌留，覽表殞絕，乃許。

translations.literal: ' At that time Suzong's illness was lingering near death; reading the memorial he collapsed as if dead, then granted it.
translations.idiomatic: ' Suzong was then gravely ill; reading the memorial he nearly fainted, then consented.

sentences.zh: 數日，肅宗晏駕，代宗踐祚，又詔晉卿攝冢宰。

translations.literal: Several days later Suzong passed away; Daizong ascended the throne, and again ordered Jinqing to act as regent chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Days later Suzong died and Daizong succeeded; again Jinqing was ordered to serve as acting regent.

sentences.zh: 晉卿上表懇辭曰：「臣以昔者天子居喪之時，百官聽於冢宰者，蓋君幼小，禦極事殷，情理當然。

translations.literal: Jinqing submitted a memorial earnestly declining, saying: 'Your servant considers that in former times when the Son of Heaven dwelt in mourning, the hundred officials listened to the regent chancellor—this was because the ruler was young and small, and assuming the pinnacle affairs were pressing; reason and circumstance made it so.
translations.idiomatic: Jinqing memorialized again in earnest refusal: 'In former times, when an emperor mourned in seclusion the hundred officials took orders from a regent because the ruler was a child and affairs of state were pressing—that was only reasonable.

sentences.zh: 沿革不一，今古異同，而周武、漢文，合於通變，垂範作則，可舉而行。

translations.literal: Continuity and change are not uniform; present and past differ in sameness and difference; yet King Wu of Zhou and Emperor Wen of Han accorded with adapting through change, handed down models and made standards that can be raised up and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Precedent varies with the age, yet King Wu of Zhou and Emperor Wen of Han adapted ritual to circumstance and left models we may follow.

sentences.zh: 又士或墨缞，時遇金革，豈非銜恤，謂義在斷恩。

translations.literal: Moreover scholars sometimes wore ink mourning dress; when they encountered metal and weapons, was this not holding grief in the breast—meaning that righteousness lies in cutting off private feeling?
translations.idiomatic: Scholars sometimes wore plain mourning garb yet took up arms when the state was threatened—grief held in the heart, but duty required setting private feeling aside.

sentences.zh: 且百善之至，無加於孝也，其有容瘁心絕，指景悼生，此匹夫守節之常情，殊王者嗣續之大計。

translations.literal: Moreover of the hundred virtues the utmost, none surpasses filial piety; yet when one has haggard appearance and heart cut off, pointing to the scene and mourning life—this is the constant feeling of a common man guarding integrity, quite different from the great plan of a king continuing the succession.
translations.idiomatic: Filial piety is the highest of virtues, yet wasting away in grief and mourning one's own life is the conduct of a private man—not the great design of a king who must continue the dynastic line.

sentences.zh: 昨二十日，陛下於大行皇帝柩前即位，是承先帝遺顧之言，亦前代不易之典。

translations.literal: Yesterday, the twentieth day, Your Majesty ascended the throne before the bier of the late emperor—this carries out the late emperor's parting charge and is also an unchanging canon of former ages.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty days ago Your Majesty took the throne before the late emperor's bier—fulfilling his dying charge and following an unchanging precedent of former dynasties.

sentences.zh: 則知所略不為害，所存是適權，防威滅端，所利者大。

translations.literal: Then one knows what is set aside does no harm, what is preserved is fitting expedient authority, guarding against awe and extinguishing beginnings—the benefit is great.
translations.idiomatic: What is set aside does no harm; what is preserved serves timely expedience—guarding against peril at its root brings the greatest benefit.

sentences.zh: 陛下因心純至，天地明察。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's responding heart is pure and utmost; Heaven and Earth see clearly.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's filial heart is pure and sincere—Heaven and Earth witness it.

sentences.zh: 伏以報劬勞之恩，申罔極之思，終身之痛，豈計朝夕！

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully considers that repaying the grace of toil and labor, expressing thoughts without limit, lifelong pain—how could one reckon by morning and evening!
translations.idiomatic: To repay parental toil and express boundless grief is a lifelong sorrow—not a matter of days alone!

sentences.zh: 但以一日之內，萬務在中，須達宸聰，始成國政。

translations.literal: Yet within a single day the myriad affairs are at the center; one must reach the imperial ear before state government can be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Yet within a single day ten thousand affairs demand the emperor's ear—only then can government proceed.

sentences.zh: 百僚萬姓及僧道耆壽等，相顧聚言，以臣老且無能，愚豈測聖，況久無居攝，臣不敢奉詔。

translations.literal: The hundred officials, myriad people, and monks, Daoists, and elders and the aged alike looked at one another and gathered in speech, saying your servant is old and without ability—how could stupidity measure the sage? Moreover there has long been no regency; your servant dare not accept the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Officials, commoners, monks, and elders alike declare that I am old and incompetent—how could such a fool measure a sage emperor? Regency has long been obsolete; I dare not accept the mandate.

sentences.zh: 特乞陛下遵遺命，三日而政。

translations.literal: I especially beg Your Majesty to follow the testamentary command and govern after three days.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty especially to follow the testament and assume governance after three days.

sentences.zh: 臣博聽眾情，不勝懇願，伏望割痛抑哀，則天下悲幸。

translations.literal: Your servant has broadly listened to the multitude's feelings and cannot bear the earnest wish; I bow and hope you will cut off pain and restrain grief—then all under Heaven will grieve and rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: Having heard the people's voice everywhere, I cannot contain my earnest plea: restrain your grief, and the realm will be overwhelmed with sorrow and joy alike.

sentences.zh: 」上號泣從之。

translations.literal: ' The emperor wailed and wept and followed it.
translations.idiomatic: ' The emperor wept aloud and assented.

sentences.zh: 時晉卿年已衰暮，又患兩足，上特許肩輿至中書，入閣不趨，累日一視事。

translations.literal: At that time Jinqing's years were already declining into old age and he also suffered in both feet; the emperor specially permitted a shoulder litter to the Secretariat, entering the pavilion without hurrying, and for many days handling affairs once.
translations.idiomatic: Jinqing was by then elderly and afflicted in both legs; the emperor specially allowed him a sedan chair to the Secretariat, excused him from hurrying into court, and let him conduct business only every few days.

sentences.zh: 歷三朝，皆以謹密見稱。

translations.literal: Through three reigns he was all praised for cautious secrecy.
translations.idiomatic: Across three reigns he was praised for discretion and reliability.

sentences.zh: 廣德初，吐蕃寇長安。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangde, the Tibetans raided Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangde era Tibetans raided Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 晉卿時病臥於私第，蕃聞之，輿入逼脅，晉卿閉口不言，賊不敢害。

translations.literal: Jinqing at the time lay ill in his private residence; the Tibetans heard of it, entered by litter to coerce him, Jinqing closed his mouth and did not speak, and the bandits did not dare harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Jinqing lay ill at home; the Tibetans heard of him, came in a litter to coerce him, but he would not speak—and the raiders did not dare harm him.

sentences.zh: 及上自陜至，冊為太保，罷知政事，又詔以太保致仕。

translations.literal: When the emperor came from Shan, he was enfeoffed Grand Guardian, ceased managing state affairs, and was again ordered to retire as Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned from Shan, Jinqing was enfeoffed grand guardian, relieved of administrative duties, and ordered to retire in that rank.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年四月薨。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Yongtai he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth month of Yongtai 1.

sentences.zh: 輟朝三日，令京兆少尹一員護喪事，緣葬諸物並官給，賻絹布五百段、米粟五百石。

translations.literal: Court was halted three days; one Vice Director of the Capital was ordered to oversee funeral affairs; all items for the funeral were supplied by the government; condolence gifts of five hundred bolts of silk and cloth and five hundred piculs of grain were given.
translations.idiomatic: Court mourning lasted three days; a vice director of the capital oversaw the funeral; all burial goods were supplied by the state; and five hundred bolts of silk and five hundred piculs of grain were granted as condolence gifts.

sentences.zh: 太常議謚曰「懿獻」。

translations.literal: The Director of Ceremonies deliberated on the posthumous name, saying 'Yi Xian.'
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Ceremonies proposed the posthumous name Yi Xian ('Benevolent and Offering').

sentences.zh: 初，晉卿東都留守，引用大理評事元載為推官。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jinqing was Eastern Capital Regent, he employed Yuan Zai, Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review, as investigating officer.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while regent of the Eastern Capital, Jinqing had appointed Yuan Zai, an evaluator in the Court of Judicial Review, as his investigating officer.

sentences.zh: 至是載為中書侍郎、平章事，懷舊恩，諷有司改謚曰文貞。

translations.literal: By this time Zai was Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-ordinating Grand Councillor; cherishing old grace, he hinted to the responsible offices to change the posthumous name to Wen Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yuan Zai was vice director of the Secretariat and chief councillor; remembering old kindness, he prompted the authorities to change the posthumous name to Wen Zhen ('Cultured and Upright').

sentences.zh: 大歷七年，令配享肅宗廟庭。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Dali he was ordered to share sacrifice in Suzong's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali year 7 he was granted a place in the sacrifices at Suzong's temple.

sentences.zh: =裴冕=裴冕，河東人也，為河東冠族。

translations.literal: = Pei Mian = Pei Mian was a man of Hedong and was the leading clan of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: — Pei Mian — Pei Mian was a native of Hedong and belonged to the region's foremost clan.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，以門廕再遷渭南縣尉，以吏道聞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, through hereditary privilege he was twice transferred to magistrate of Weinan and became known for the way of clerical administration.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianbao era he rose through hereditary privilege to magistrate of Weinan and won a reputation for administrative skill.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞王鉷充京畿采訪使，表為判官。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Wang Hong served as Capital Region Investigation Commissioner and recommended him as administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor-in-Chief Wang Hong served as capital-region investigation commissioner he recommended Mian as his administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 遷監察御史，歷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Investigating Censor and successively served as Attending Censor in the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to investigating censor and then served as palace attending censor.

sentences.zh: 冕雖無學術，守職通明，果於臨事，鉷甚委之。

translations.literal: Mian although without learning, in guarding his post was penetratingly clear, decisive in facing affairs, and Hong greatly entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Though without scholarly training, Mian was lucid in office and resolute in action; Wang Hong relied on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 及鉷得罪伏法，時宰臣李林甫方竊權柄，人鹹懼之，鉷賓佐數百，不敢窺鉷門。

translations.literal: When Hong was guilty and executed by law, at that time Chief Councillor Li Linfu was just usurping power; people all feared him; Hong's guest aides numbered several hundred and did not dare peek at Hong's gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Hong was executed, Chief Councillor Li Linfu held power and all feared him; Hong's hundreds of staff did not dare even approach his gate.

sentences.zh: 冕獨收鉷屍，親自護喪，瘞於近郊，冕自是知名。

translations.literal: Mian alone collected Hong's corpse, personally guarded the funeral, and buried him in the near suburbs; from this Mian became known.
translations.idiomatic: Mian alone recovered Hong's body, personally conducted the funeral, and buried him in the suburbs—after which Mian became widely known.

sentences.zh: 河西節度使哥舒翰表為行軍司馬，累遷員外郎中。

translations.literal: Hexi Military Commissioner Geshu Han recommended him as campaigning marshal and he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi commissioner Geshu Han recommended him as campaigning marshal; he rose in turn to vice director.

sentences.zh: 玄宗幸蜀，至益昌郡，遙詔太子充天下兵馬元帥，以冕為御史中丞兼左庶子，為之副。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong went to Shu, reaching Yichang Commandery; from afar he edicted the Heir Apparent to serve as Commander-in-Chief of all armies and horses under Heaven, with Mian as Censor-in-Chief and concurrently Left Guardian of the Heir Apparent as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong fled to Shu and reached Yichang, he issued a distant edict naming the crown prince commander of all forces under heaven, with Mian as censor-in-chief and left guardian of the heir as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 是時，冕為河西行軍司馬，授御史中丞，詔赴朝廷。

translations.literal: At that time Mian was Hexi campaigning marshal; he was appointed Censor-in-Chief and ordered by edict to proceed to court.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was then campaigning marshal in Hexi; appointed censor-in-chief, he was ordered to proceed to court.

sentences.zh: 遇太子於平涼，具陳事勢，勸之朔方，亟入靈武。

translations.literal: He met the Heir Apparent at Pingliang, fully stated the situation of affairs, urged him toward Shuofang, and urgently to enter Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: He met the crown prince at Pingliang, laid out the strategic situation in full, urged him toward Shuofang, and pressed him to enter Lingwu at once.

sentences.zh: 冕與杜鴻漸、崔漪等勸進曰：「主上厭勤大位，南幸蜀川，宗社神器，須有所歸，天意人事，不可固違。

translations.literal: Mian with Du Hongjian, Cui Yi, and others urged advancement, saying: 'The sovereign has grown weary of the toil of the great position and gone south to favor Shu; the altars of state and the sacred vessel must have someone to return to them—Heaven's intent and human affairs cannot be stubbornly opposed.
translations.idiomatic: Mian, Du Hongjian, Cui Yi, and others urged the prince to take the throne: 'The emperor has grown weary of rule and gone south to Shu; the altars of state and the imperial regalia must have a home—Heaven's will and human necessity cannot be defied.

sentences.zh: 若逡巡退讓，失億兆心，則大事去矣！

translations.literal: If you hesitate and yield in retreat, losing the hearts of the hundred millions, then the great affair is gone!
translations.idiomatic: If you hesitate and step aside, you will lose the hearts of the people—and the great cause will be lost!

sentences.zh: 臣等猶知之，況賢智乎！

translations.literal: We your servants still know this—how much more the worthy and wise!
translations.idiomatic: Even we understand this—how much more must the wise among men!

sentences.zh: 」太子曰：「南平寇逆，奉迎鑾輿，退居儲貳，侍膳左右，豈不樂哉！

translations.literal: ' The Heir Apparent said: 'To pacify the south and subdue rebels, welcome back the imperial carriage, withdraw to the position of heir, and attend meals at the sovereign's side—would this not be joy!
translations.idiomatic: ' The crown prince replied, 'To pacify the south, defeat the rebels, welcome back the imperial carriage, and then serve at my father's side as heir apparent—what could be happier than that!

sentences.zh: 公等何言之過也？

translations.literal: Why do you gentlemen speak so excessively?
translations.idiomatic: Your words go too far, gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 」冕與杜鴻漸又進曰：「殿下藉累聖之資，有天下之表。

translations.literal: ' Mian and Du Hongjian again advanced, saying: 'Your Highness relies on the accumulated virtue of successive sages and has the bearing to rule all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: ' Mian and Du Hongjian pressed again: 'Your Highness inherits the accumulated virtue of successive sage emperors and bears the countenance of one who should rule the realm.

sentences.zh: 元貞萬國，二十余年，殷憂啟聖，正在今日。

translations.literal: Sincere and upright over ten thousand states for more than twenty years—deep sorrow giving birth to sageliness is precisely today.
translations.idiomatic: For more than twenty years the dynasty has held the realm in sincere devotion; out of deep crisis a sage ruler must emerge—and that moment is today.

sentences.zh: 所從殿下六軍將士，皆關輔百姓，日夜思歸。

translations.literal: The six-army officers and soldiers who follow Your Highness are all common people of the Guan region and the capital approaches; day and night they think of returning home.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers of the six armies who follow you are all men of the capital region who long day and night to return home.

sentences.zh: 大軍一散，不可復集，不如因而撫之以從眾，臣等敢以死請。

translations.literal: Once the great army disperses it cannot be gathered again; better to take advantage of the moment and comfort them to follow the multitude—we your servants dare beg with our lives.
translations.idiomatic: Once the army disperses it cannot be reassembled; accept the throne now to hold the men together—we beg this at the risk of our lives.

sentences.zh: 」凡勸進五上，乃依。

translations.literal: ' In all they urged advancement five times before he assented.
translations.idiomatic: ' After five rounds of urging, the prince at last agreed.

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位，以定策功，遷中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事，倚以為政。

translations.literal: When Suzong ascended the throne, for merit in settling the strategy he was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-ordinating Grand Councillor with the Secretariat Chancellery, and relied on for government.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong took the throne, Mian was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat and chief councillor for his role in the succession, and the emperor relied on him to govern.

sentences.zh: 冕性忠勤，悉心奉公，稍得人心。

translations.literal: Mian's nature was loyal and diligent; he devoted his heart to serving the public and gradually won people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was loyal and diligent, devoted himself wholly to public service, and gradually won popular regard.

sentences.zh: 然不識大體，以聚人曰財，乃下令賣官鬻爵，度尼僧道士，以儲積為務。

translations.literal: Yet he did not understand the great substance; taking gathering people to mean wealth, he then ordered selling offices and peddling ranks, ordaining nuns, monks, and Daoist priests, making accumulation his task.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he lacked a grasp of larger policy; believing that amassing people meant amassing wealth, he ordered the sale of offices and ranks, ordained nuns, monks, and Daoist priests, and made hoarding his chief concern.

sentences.zh: 人不願者，科令就之，其價益賤，事轉為弊。

translations.literal: Those who did not wish it were assessed and ordered to comply; the price grew ever cheaper, and the affair turned into harm.
translations.idiomatic: Those who resisted were compelled by statute to comply; prices fell ever lower, and the policy became a public scandal.

sentences.zh: 肅宗移幸鳳翔，罷冕知政事，遷右僕射。

translations.literal: When Suzong moved his favor to Fengxiang, Mian was removed from managing state affairs and transferred to Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong moved the court to Fengxiang, Mian was relieved of administrative duties and made right vice director.

sentences.zh: 兩京平，以功封冀國公，食實封五百戶。

translations.literal: When the two capitals were pacified, for merit he was enfeoffed Duke of Ji with five hundred households of substantive fief.
translations.idiomatic: After the two capitals were recovered he was enfeoffed as Duke of Ji with a substantive fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋加御史大夫、成都尹，充劍南西川節度使。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Censor-in-Chief, Prefect of Chengdu, and Military Commissioner of Jiannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon also made censor-in-chief, prefect of Chengdu, and military commissioner of Jiannan West.

sentences.zh: 又入為右僕射。

translations.literal: He again entered the capital as Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He later returned to the capital as right vice director.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，與裴遵慶等並集賢待制。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai he and Pei Zunqing and others were together Academicians Awaiting Imperial Orders at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongtai 1 he and Pei Zunqing and others were appointed academicians awaiting orders at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 代宗求舊，拜冕兼御史大夫，充護山陵使。

translations.literal: Daizong sought old ministers and appointed Mian concurrently Censor-in-Chief, serving as Commissioner for Guarding the Imperial Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong, seeking veteran ministers, appointed Mian concurrent censor-in-chief and commissioner for guarding the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 冕以幸臣李輔國權盛，將附之，乃表輔國親昵術士中書舍人劉烜充山陵使判官。

translations.literal: Mian, because favored minister Li Fuguo's power was flourishing and wishing to attach to him, memorialized that Fuguo's intimate associate, the technician Drafting Attendant Liu Xuan, should serve as administrative aide to the mausoleum commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to curry favor with the powerful favorite Li Fuguo, Mian recommended Fuguo's intimate, the drafting attendant and occultist Liu Xuan, as administrative aide on the tomb commission.

sentences.zh: 烜坐法，冕坐貶施州刺史。

translations.literal: Xuan was guilty by law; Mian was implicated and demoted to Prefect of Shi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan was convicted by law, Mian was implicated and demoted to prefect of Shi.

sentences.zh: 數月，移澧州刺史，復征為左僕射。

translations.literal: Several months later he was moved to Prefect of Li Prefecture and again summoned as Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Months later he was transferred to prefect of Li and again summoned as left vice director.

sentences.zh: 元載秉政。

translations.literal: Yuan Zai held government power.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai held the reins of government.

sentences.zh: 載為新平縣尉，王鉷辟在巡內，冕常引之，載頗德冕。

translations.literal: Zai had been magistrate of Xinping; Wang Hong recruited him within his circuit inspection, and Mian often recommended him—Zai was quite grateful to Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Zai had once been magistrate of Xinping; Wang Hong recruited him on his inspection tours, and Mian had often advanced him—Zai remained deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 會宰臣杜鴻漸卒，載遂舉冕代之。

translations.literal: When Chief Councillor Du Hongjian died, Zai then recommended Mian to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chief Councillor Du Hongjian died, Zai recommended Mian to replace him.

sentences.zh: 冕時已衰瘵，載以其順己，引為同列。

translations.literal: Mian at that time was already declining with illness; Zai, because he complied with himself, brought him in as a fellow councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was by then gravely ill; Zai, knowing he would not oppose him, brought him onto the council as a fellow minister.

sentences.zh: 受命之際，蹈舞絕倒，載趨而扶起，代為謝詞。

translations.literal: At the moment of receiving the mandate he stamped and danced and collapsed utterly; Zai hurried forward to raise him and spoke the words of thanks in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: At his investiture Mian stamped, danced, and collapsed; Zai rushed forward to lift him and delivered the thanks on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 冕兼掌兵權留守之任，俸錢每月二千余貫。

translations.literal: Mian concurrently held military authority and the duty of regent; his salary was more than two thousand strings per month.
translations.idiomatic: Mian also held military authority and the regency; his monthly salary exceeded two thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 性本侈靡，好尚車服及營珍饌，名馬在櫪，直數百金者常十數。

translations.literal: His nature was fundamentally extravagant; he loved carriages, robes, and preparing rare delicacies; famous horses in the stable worth several hundred in gold were commonly a dozen or more.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was extravagant, fond of fine carriages and robes and elaborate feasts; a dozen famous horses worth hundreds of gold each stood in his stables.

sentences.zh: 每會賓友，滋味品數，坐客有昧於名者。

translations.literal: Whenever he gathered guests and friends, the flavors and varieties of dishes—among seated guests there were those ignorant of the names.
translations.idiomatic: At every banquet for guests the dishes were so numerous and exotic that some guests could not even name what they were eating.

sentences.zh: 自創巾子，其狀新奇，市肆因而效之，呼為「僕射樣」。

translations.literal: He himself created a headcloth, its form novel; market shops thereupon imitated it, calling it the 'Vice Director style.'
translations.idiomatic: He invented a new style of headcloth so striking that shops across the city copied it and called it the 'vice director's style.'

sentences.zh: 初代鴻漸，小吏以俸錢文簿白之，冕顧子弟，喜見於色，其嗜利若此。

translations.literal: When he first replaced Hongjian, a petty clerk reported the salary accounts in writing; Mian looked at his sons and nephews, joy visible on his face—his craving for profit was like this.
translations.idiomatic: When he first replaced Hongjian, a clerk presented the salary ledger; Mian glanced at his sons and nephews with visible delight—such was his love of gain.

sentences.zh: 拜職未盈月，卒，大歷四年十二月也。

translations.literal: He had not completed a full month in the post when he died—in the twelfth month of the fourth year of Dali.
translations.idiomatic: He had held office less than a month when he died, in the twelfth month of Dali 4.

sentences.zh: 上悼之，輟朝三日，贈太尉，賻制五百匹、粟五百石。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned him; court was halted three days; he was posthumously granted Grand Marshal; condolence gifts of five hundred bolts and five hundred piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him with three days of court suspension, posthumously granted him grand marshal, and sent five hundred bolts of silk and five hundred piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: =裴遵慶=裴遵慶，絳州聞喜人也。

translations.literal: = Pei Zunqing = Pei Zunqing was a man of Wenxi in Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: — Pei Zunqing — Pei Zunqing was a native of Wenxi in Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 代襲冠冕，為河東著族。

translations.literal: For generations they inherited caps and coronets and were a distinguished clan of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the family held high rank and were a leading clan of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 遵慶志氣深厚，機鑒敏達，自幼強學，博涉載籍，謹身晦跡，不幹當世之務。

translations.literal: Zunqing's will and spirit were deep and thick, his insight and discernment keen and penetrating; from youth he studied strenuously, broadly traversed written records, guarded himself and concealed his traces, and did not meddle in the affairs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Zunqing was deep-spirited and keen-witted; from youth he studied hard and read widely, kept a low profile, and avoided entanglement in contemporary politics.

sentences.zh: 以門廕累授潞府司法參軍，時年已老，未為人所知。

translations.literal: Through hereditary privilege he was repeatedly appointed Judicial Administrator of Lu Prefecture; at the time he was already old and not yet known to people.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege he rose to judicial administrator in Lu Prefecture, but he was already elderly and still unknown to the wider world.

sentences.zh: 隨調吏部，授大理寺丞，剖斷刑獄，舉正綱條，理行始著。

translations.literal: Following reassignment at the Ministry of Personnel he was appointed Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review, dissecting and deciding criminal cases, upholding the main statutes—his governing conduct first became notable.
translations.idiomatic: On routine reassignment at the Ministry of Personnel he was made assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review, where his handling of criminal cases and enforcement of statutes first brought his talent to notice.

sentences.zh: 遷司門員外、吏部員外郎，專判南曹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Gate Office and Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel, exclusively judging the Southern Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Gate Office and the Ministry of Personnel, with sole charge of the Southern Bureau.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，海內無事，九流輻輳會府，每歲吏部選人，動盈萬數。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era the realm within the seas was without affairs; the nine streams converged like spokes at the capital offices; each year the Ministry of Personnel's candidates commonly exceeded ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao era the empire was at peace and candidates of every stripe thronged the capital; each year's civil-service examinations drew well over ten thousand applicants.

sentences.zh: 遵慶敏識強記，精核文簿，詳而不滯，時稱吏事第一，由是大知名。

translations.literal: Zunqing was keen in recognition and strong in memory, finely examining documents and ledgers, detailed yet without stagnation; at the time he was called first in clerical affairs—from this he became greatly renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Zunqing was quick-witted with a prodigious memory, mastered documents with meticulous care yet without delay, and was acclaimed the foremost administrator of his day—winning wide renown.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，楊國忠當國，出不附己者例為外官，遵慶亦出為郡守。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao Yang Guozhong held the state; those who did not attach to him were routinely made outer officials—Zunqing also went out as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Tianbao, Yang Guozhong dominated the court and routinely posted opponents to provincial office; Zunqing too was sent out as a prefect.

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位，征拜給事中、尚書右丞、吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Suzong ascended the throne he was summoned and appointed Drafting Attendant, Right Assistant in the Secretariat, and Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong took the throne, Zunqing was summoned as drafting attendant, right assistant director of the secretariat, and vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 恭儉克己，遲重謹密，頗有時望。

translations.literal: Respectful, frugal, and restraining himself; slow, weighty, cautious, and secretive—he had considerable contemporary renown.
translations.idiomatic: Respectful, frugal, and self-restrained, deliberate and discreet, he enjoyed considerable standing at court.

sentences.zh: 上元中，蕭華輔政，素知遵慶，每奏見，累稱之，遷黃門侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the Shangyuan era Xiao Hua assisted in government, having long known Zunqing; at each memorial audience he repeatedly praised him; he was transferred to Vice Director of the Palace Gate and Co-ordinating Grand Councillor with the Secretariat Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shangyuan era, Chief Councillor Xiao Hua, who had long known Zunqing's worth, repeatedly praised him at audience and had him promoted to vice director of the palace gate and chief councillor.

sentences.zh: 廣德初，仆固懷恩阻兵汾上，指中官為詞，上以遵慶忠純，特遣往汾州宣慰懷恩。

translations.literal: Early in Guangde Pugu Huai'en blocked the army on the Fen, using eunuchs as his pretext; the emperor, because Zunqing was loyal and pure, specially sent him to Fen Prefecture to proclaim comfort to Huai'en.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangde, Pugu Huai'en held troops on the Fen River and blamed the eunuchs; the emperor, trusting Zunqing's loyalty, specially dispatched him to Fen Prefecture to reassure Huai'en.

sentences.zh: 遵慶既見懷恩，具陳朝旨，懷恩引過聽命，將隨遵慶朝謁，為副將範誌誠以邪說惑之，懷恩遂以懼死為詞。

translations.literal: After Zunqing met Huai'en he fully stated the court's intent; Huai'en acknowledged fault and obeyed, about to follow Zunqing to court audience, but his deputy Fan Zhicheng confused him with heterodox talk—Huai'en then used fear of death as his plea.
translations.idiomatic: When Zunqing met Huai'en he laid out the court's intent in full; Huai'en acknowledged his errors and agreed to accompany Zunqing to court, but his deputy Fan Zhicheng swayed him with sinister counsel, and Huai'en pleaded that he feared execution.

sentences.zh: 會蕃寇陷京師，乘輿幸陜，遵慶自汾州奔赴行在。

translations.literal: When Tibetan bandits seized the capital and the imperial carriage favored Shan, Zunqing from Fen Prefecture hurried to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibetan raiders took the capital and the emperor fled to Shan, Zunqing rushed from Fen Prefecture to join the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 及乘輿還京，以遵慶為太子少傅。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital, Zunqing was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the capital, Zunqing was appointed junior tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，與裴冕等並於集賢院待制，罷知政事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai he and Pei Mian and others were together at the Hall of Assembled Worthies as Academicians Awaiting Orders, and ceased managing state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongtai 1 he and Pei Mian and others were made academicians at the Hall of Assembled Worthies and relieved of administrative duties.

sentences.zh: 尋改吏部尚書、右僕射，復知選事。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to Minister of Personnel and Right Vice Director, again managing selection affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made minister of personnel and right vice director and again put in charge of civil-service selection.

sentences.zh: 時選人天興縣尉陳琯於銓庭言詞不遜，淩突無禮，代宗詔付遵慶於省門鞭三十，貶為吉州員外司戶參軍。

translations.literal: At that time the candidate Chen Guan, magistrate of Tianxing, used insubordinate words in the selection courtyard, overbearing and without propriety; Daizong ordered him handed to Zunqing to be flogged thirty times at the ministry gate and demoted to Acting Registrar of Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the candidate Chen Guan, magistrate of Tianxing, spoke insolently at the selection courtyard, Daizong ordered Zunqing to have him flogged thirty strokes at the ministry gate and demoted to acting registrar in Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遵慶敦守儒行，老而彌謹。

translations.literal: Zunqing earnestly guarded Confucian conduct and grew more cautious in old age.
translations.idiomatic: Zunqing steadfastly upheld Confucian conduct and grew only more cautious with age.

sentences.zh: 嘗為風狂族侄撾登聞鼓告以不順，上知遵度，不省，其見信如此。

translations.literal: Once a mad clansman nephew beat the Petition Drum at the Gate of Imperial Audience and reported him for disloyalty; the emperor knew Zunqing's measure and did not investigate—such was the trust shown in him.
translations.idiomatic: Once a deranged clansman beat the petition drum at the Gate of Imperial Audience and accused him of disloyalty; the emperor, knowing Zunqing's character, paid no heed—such was the trust he enjoyed.

sentences.zh: 大歷十年十月薨於位，年九十余。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the tenth year of Dali he died in office, aged more than ninety.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the tenth month of Dali 10, aged more than ninety.

sentences.zh: 遵慶初登省郎，嘗著《王政記》，述今古禮體，識者覽之，知有公輔之量。

translations.literal: When Zunqing first rose to provincial bureau officer he once composed 'Record of Royal Government,' narrating ancient and modern ritual forms; those with discernment who read it knew he had the capacity of chief minister and assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his career as a provincial bureau officer he wrote Record of Royal Government, surveying ritual institutions past and present; readers recognized in it the makings of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 遵慶子 向子向，字傃仁，少以門廕歷官至太子司議郎。

translations.literal: Zunqing's son Xiang, styled Surén, from youth through hereditary privilege rose in office to Petition Reviewer of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Zunqing's son Xiang, courtesy name Surén, rose through hereditary privilege to petition reviewer of the heir apparent while still young.

sentences.zh: 建中初，李紓為同州刺史，奏向為從事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong Li Shu was Prefect of Tong Prefecture and memorialized Xiang as staff member.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianzhong era, when Li Shu was prefect of Tong, he recommended Xiang as his staff officer.

sentences.zh: 硃泚反，李懷光又叛河中，使其將趙貴先築壘於同州，紓來奔奉天，向領州務。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci rebelled; Li Huai'guang also rebelled in Hezhong and sent his general Zhao Guixian to build ramparts at Tong Prefecture; Shu came fleeing to Fengtian, and Xiang took charge of prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rebelled and Li Huai'guang rose in Hezhong, sending his general Zhao Guixian to fortify Tong, Shu fled to Fengtian and Xiang took charge of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貴先因脅縣尉林寶役徒板築，不及期，將斬之，吏人百姓奔竄。

translations.literal: Guixian thereupon coerced Assistant Magistrate Lin Bao to press laborers into plank construction; when the deadline was not met he was about to behead him—clerks, people, and commoners fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: Guixian forced Assistant Magistrate Lin Bao to press laborers into construction work; when the deadline was missed he was about to execute Bao, and officials and commoners fled in terror.

sentences.zh: 向即詣貴先軍壘，以逆順之理責之，貴先感悟，遂來降，故同州不陷。

translations.literal: Xiang immediately went to Guixian's military ramparts and rebuked him with the principle of rebellion and obedience; Guixian was moved to awareness and then came to surrender—therefore Tong Prefecture did not fall.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang went at once to Guixian's camp and rebuked him on the principles of loyalty and rebellion; Guixian was moved to repentance and surrendered, and Tong Prefecture was thus spared.

sentences.zh: 向由是知名。

translations.literal: From this Xiang became known.
translations.idiomatic: From this Xiang won wide renown.

sentences.zh: 累為京兆府戶曹，轉櫟陽、渭南縣令，奏課皆第一，朝廷亟聞其理行，擢為戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: He repeatedly served as Revenue Clerk of the Capital Prefecture, was transferred to magistrate of Liyang and Weinan; his memorial assessments were all first—the court quickly heard of his governing conduct and promoted him to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He served as revenue clerk in the capital prefecture and as magistrate of Liyang and Weinan, earning top ratings in every assessment; the court soon heard of his governance and promoted him to vice director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 德宗季年，天下方鎮副倅多自選於朝，防一日有變，遂就而授之節制。

translations.literal: In the late years of Dezong, deputy commissioners of the realm's military commissions were mostly chosen from the court, guarding against a sudden change one day—then they were at hand to be granted command.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Dezong's reign, deputy commissioners for the military provinces were largely chosen from the central government so that, if crisis arose, trusted men would already be in place to receive command.

sentences.zh: 向已選為太原少尹，德宗召見喻旨，尋用為行軍司馬、兼御史中丞，改汾州刺史，轉鄭州。

translations.literal: Xiang had already been selected as Junior Governor of Taiyuan; Dezong summoned him for audience and explained the intent; soon he was employed as campaigning marshal and concurrently Censor-in-Chief, changed to Prefect of Fen Prefecture, transferred to Zheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang had been selected as junior governor of Taiyuan; Dezong summoned him to explain his intentions, then appointed him campaigning marshal and concurrent censor-in-chief, later prefect of Fen and then of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 又復為太原少尹，兼河東節度副使。

translations.literal: He again became Junior Governor of Taiyuan and concurrently Deputy Military Commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as junior governor of Taiyuan and deputy military commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 改晉州刺史，充本州防禦使，遷虢州刺史。

translations.literal: He was changed to Prefect of Jin Prefecture, serving as Defense Commissioner of that prefecture, and transferred to Prefect of Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made prefect of Jin and defense commissioner of that prefecture, then transferred to prefect of Guo.

sentences.zh: 入為京兆少尹，拜同州刺史，充本州防禦使。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Junior Governor of the Capital Prefecture, was appointed Prefect of Tong Prefecture, and served as Defense Commissioner of that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital as junior governor of the metropolitan prefecture, then was appointed prefect of Tong and its defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 入為大理寺卿，出遷陜虢都防禦、觀察使。

translations.literal: He entered as Director of the Court of Judicial Review and went out transferred to Defense and Surveillance Commissioner of Shan and Guo.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as director of the Court of Judicial Review, then sent out as defense and surveillance commissioner for Shan and Guo.

sentences.zh: 三歲，拜左散騎常侍，自常侍復為大理。

translations.literal: After three years he was appointed Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry Guard; from Regular Attendant he again became Director of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he was made left regular attendant of the cavalry guard, then returned to the directorship of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 向本以名相子，以學行自飭，謹守其門風。

translations.literal: Xiang was originally the son of a famous chief minister; by learning and conduct he restrained himself and carefully guarded his family's style.
translations.idiomatic: As the son of a famous chief minister, Xiang disciplined himself through learning and conduct and carefully upheld his family's reputation.

sentences.zh: 歷官仁智推愛，利及於人。

translations.literal: In successive offices he extended benevolence and wisdom with love; benefit reached people.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he extended benevolence and wisdom, bringing benefit to those around him.

sentences.zh: 至是，以年過致政，朝廷優異，乃以吏部尚書致仕於新昌裏第。

translations.literal: By this time, because his years had passed he retired from government; the court treated him with special favor and he retired as Minister of Personnel at his residence in Xinchang Lane.
translations.idiomatic: By then, advanced in years, he retired; the court honored him with exceptional favor and allowed him to retire as minister of personnel at his home in Xinchang Lane.

sentences.zh: 內外支屬百余人，向所得俸祿，必同其費，及領外任，亦挈而隨之。

translations.literal: Inner and outer branch kin numbered more than a hundred; whatever salary Xiang received he always shared the expense, and when he took outer posts he also brought them along.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred kinsmen of the inner and outer branches depended on him; he always shared his salary with them, and when he took provincial posts he brought them along.

sentences.zh: 有孤煢疾苦不能自恤，向尤周給，至今稱其孝睦焉。

translations.literal: When there were orphans and the solitary, the ill and suffering who could not care for themselves, Xiang especially provided roundly—to this day they praise his filial piety and harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Orphans, the destitute, and the sick who could not care for themselves he especially supported; to this day he is praised for filial devotion and family harmony.

sentences.zh: 大和四年九月卒，年八十。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Dahe he died, aged eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth month of Dahe 4, aged eighty.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as junior tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 向子 寅子寅，登進士第，累官至御史大夫卒。

translations.literal: Xiang's son Yin; Yin passed the jinshi examination and through successive offices reached Censor-in-Chief before dying.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang's son Yin passed the jinshi examination and rose through the ranks to censor-in-chief before his death.

sentences.zh: 寅子 樞子樞，字紀聖，咸通十二年登進士第。

translations.literal: Yin's son Shu; Shu, styled Jisheng, in the twelfth year of Xiantong passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's son Shu, courtesy name Jisheng, passed the jinshi examination in Xiantong 12.

sentences.zh: 宰相杜審權出鎮河中，辟為從事，得秘書省校書郎，再遷藍田尉。

translations.literal: Chief Councillor Du Shenquan went out to command Hezhong and recruited him as staff member; he obtained Collator of the Secretariat and was again transferred to magistrate of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: When Chief Councillor Du Shenquan took command of Hezhong he recruited Shu as staff officer; Shu became collator of the Secretariat and later magistrate of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 直弘文館。

translations.literal: He served directly at the Hall of Expansive Culture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a direct attendant at the Hall of Expansive Culture.

sentences.zh: 大學士王鐸深知之，鐸罷相失職，樞亦久之不調。

translations.literal: Grand Academician Wang Duo deeply knew him; when Duo was removed from the chancellorship and lost his post, Shu also for a long time received no reassignment.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Academician Wang Duo thought highly of him; when Duo lost the chancellorship, Shu too went long without reassignment.

sentences.zh: 從僖宗幸蜀，中丞李煥奏為殿中侍御史，遷起居郎。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Xizong in favoring Shu; Vice Censor Li Huan memorialized him as Attending Censor in the Palace and he was transferred to Attendant for Drafting the Imperial Diary.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Xizong to Shu; Vice Censor Li Huan recommended him as palace attending censor, and he was promoted to attendant for drafting the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 中和初，王鐸復見用，以舊恩徙為鄭滑掌書記、檢校司封郎中，賜金紫，入朝歷兵、吏二員外郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhonghe Wang Duo was again employed; because of old grace he was moved to Secretary of Zheng and Hua, Acting Director in the Office for Enfeoffment, granted gold and purple; entering court he successively served as Vice Director in the Ministries of War and Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhonghe era Wang Duo returned to power and, remembering old ties, appointed Shu secretary at Zheng-Hua and acting director in the Office for Enfeoffment, with the gold-and-purple insignia; recalled to court he served as vice director in the ministries of War and Personnel.

sentences.zh: 龍紀初，擢拜給事中，改京兆尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longji he was promoted and appointed Drafting Attendant, changed to Governor of the Capital Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Longji era he was promoted to drafting attendant and then made governor of the metropolitan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宰相孔緯尤深獎遇。

translations.literal: Chief Councillor Kong Wei especially deeply rewarded and favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councillor Kong Wei especially favored and promoted him.

sentences.zh: 大順中，緯以用兵無功貶官，樞坐累為右庶子，尋出為歙州刺史。

translations.literal: In Dazhun Wei was demoted for military use without achievement; Shu was implicated and made Right Guardian of the Heir Apparent, soon sent out as Prefect of She Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During Dazhun, when Wei was demoted for military failure, Shu was implicated and made right guardian of the heir apparent, then sent out as prefect of She.

sentences.zh: 乾寧初，入為右散騎常侍，從昭宗幸華州，為汴州宣諭使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianning he entered as Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry Guard, followed Emperor Zhaozong in favoring Hua Prefecture, and served as Proclamation and Comfort Commissioner to Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianning he returned as right regular attendant of the cavalry guard, accompanied Zhaozong to Hua Prefecture, and served as imperial envoy to Bian.

sentences.zh: 初，樞自歙州罷郡歸朝，路經大梁，時硃全忠兵威已振，樞以兄事之，全忠由是重之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shu left his prefecture at She and returned to court, his route passed through Daliang; at that time Zhu Quanzhong's military prestige was already rising—Shu treated him as an elder brother, and Quanzhong thereby valued him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu left the prefecture of She and returned to court, his route passed through Daliang; Zhu Quanzhong's military power was already formidable, and Shu treated him as an elder brother—whereupon Quanzhong came to esteem him.

sentences.zh: 及樞傳詔，全忠皆稟朝旨，獻奉相繼，昭宗甚悅，遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Shu transmitted the edict, Quanzhong all followed court intent; tribute offerings followed in succession; Zhaozong was greatly pleased and transferred him to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu delivered the imperial edict, Quanzhong complied with the court's wishes and sent tribute in succession; Zhaozong was greatly pleased and promoted Shu to vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 時崔胤專政，亦倚全忠，二人因是相結，改樞吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: At that time Cui Yin monopolized government and also relied on Quanzhong; the two men thereby joined together and changed Shu to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin then dominated the government and also relied on Quanzhong; the two allied, and Shu was made vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 未幾，換戶部侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Before long he was exchanged to Vice Minister of the Household and Co-ordinating Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to vice minister of the household and appointed chief councillor.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，昭宗幸華州，崔胤貶官，樞亦為工部尚書。

translations.literal: That winter Zhaozong favored Hua Prefecture; Cui Yin was demoted, and Shu also became Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when Zhaozong went to Hua and Cui Yin was demoted, Shu was made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 天子自岐下還宮，以樞檢校右僕射、同平章事，出為廣南節度使。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven returned to the palace from below Qi, Shu was made Acting Right Vice Director and Co-ordinating Grand Councillor, and sent out as Military Commissioner of Guangnan.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned from Qi to the capital, Shu was made acting right vice director and chief councillor, then sent out as military commissioner of Guangnan.

sentences.zh: 制出，硃全忠保薦之，言樞有經世才，不可棄之嶺表，尋復拜門下侍郎，監修國史，累兼吏部尚書，判度支。

translations.literal: When the appointment was issued, Zhu Quanzhong protected and recommended him, saying Shu had talent to order the age and could not be abandoned to the southern mountains; soon he was again appointed Vice Director of the Gate Department, supervising compilation of the national history, cumulatively also Minister of Personnel, judging the Department of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When the appointment was issued, Zhu Quanzhong intervened, declaring that Shu had talent to govern the age and must not be sent to the far south; Shu was soon recalled as vice director of the gate department, supervisor of the national history, and concurrently minister of personnel with charge of the treasury.

sentences.zh: 崔胤誅，以全忠素厚，相位如故。

translations.literal: When Cui Yin was executed, because Quanzhong had long been thick with him, his chancellorship remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Yin was executed, Shu retained his chancellorship through his long-standing ties to Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 從昭宗遷洛陽，駐蹕陜州，進右僕射、弘文館大學士、太清宮使，充諸道鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: He followed Zhaozong in moving to Luoyang, halted the imperial progress at Shan Prefecture, was advanced to Right Vice Director, Grand Academician of the Hall of Expansive Culture, Commissioner of the Great Pure Palace, and served as Salt and Iron Transport Commissioner for all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Zhaozong to Luoyang and, when the court halted at Shan, was promoted to right vice director, grand academician of the Hall of Expansive Culture, commissioner of the Great Pure Palace, and salt-and-iron transport commissioner for all circuits.

sentences.zh: 哀帝初嗣位，柳璨用事，全忠嘗奏用牙將張廷範為太常卿，諸相議，樞曰：「廷範勛臣，幸有方鎮節鉞之命，何藉樂卿？

translations.literal: When Emperor Aidi first succeeded to the throne, Liu Can wielded power; Quanzhong once memorialized to employ his military officer Zhang Tingfan as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; the chief ministers deliberated; Shu said: 'Tingfan is a meritorious minister—fortunately there may be a command of military commission and ceremonial axe for a frontier post; why rely on Director of Music?
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Aidi first succeeded, Liu Can held power; Quanzhong memorialized to appoint his military officer Zhang Tingfan director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. The chief ministers debated; Shu said, 'Tingfan is a meritorious officer who might well receive a frontier military commission—why does he need the directorship of the Court of Sacrifices?

sentences.zh: 恐非元帥梁王之旨。

translations.literal: I fear this is not the intent of the commander-in-chief, Prince of Liang.'
translations.idiomatic: I fear this is not the intent of the commander-in-chief, the Prince of Liang.'

sentences.zh: 」乃持之不下。

translations.literal: ' He thereupon held to his position and would not issue the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: ' He held firm and refused to issue the appointment.

sentences.zh: 俄而全忠聞樞言，謂賓佐曰：「吾常以裴十四器識真純，不入浮薄之伍，觀此議論，本態露矣。

translations.literal: Soon Quanzhong heard Shu's words and said to his guest aides: 'I always took Pei the Fourteenth's capacity and insight to be truly pure, not entering the ranks of the frivolous and shallow—viewing this discussion, his true nature is exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Quanzhong heard what Shu had said and told his staff, 'I always thought Pei the Fourteenth was genuinely upright and above the shallow crowd—but this argument shows his true colors.

sentences.zh: 」切齒含怒。

translations.literal: ' He gnashed his teeth and harbored anger.
translations.idiomatic: ' He gnashed his teeth in fury.

sentences.zh: 柳璨聞全忠言，尋希旨罷樞相位，和陵祔享，拜尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Liu Can heard Quanzhong's words and soon, to please his intent, removed Shu from the chancellorship; for the joint offering at the imperial tomb he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can, hearing Quanzhong's words, soon pleased his intent by removing Shu from the chancellorship; Shu was made left vice director of the secretariat for the joint tomb offering.

sentences.zh: 五月，責授朝散大夫、登州刺史，尋再貶瀧州司戶。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he was punished and granted Gentleman for Dispersing at Court and Prefect of Deng Prefecture; soon he was again demoted to Registrar of Long Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he was demoted to gentleman for dispersing at court and prefect of Deng; soon he was demoted again to registrar in Long Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 六月十一日，行及滑州，全忠遣人殺之於白馬驛，投屍於河，時年六十五。

translations.literal: On the eleventh day of the sixth month, when his journey reached Hua Prefecture, Quanzhong sent men to kill him at Baima Post Station and cast his corpse into the river; at the time he was sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: On the eleventh day of the sixth month, when he reached Hua Prefecture, Quanzhong had him killed at Baima Post Station and his body thrown into the river; he was sixty-five.

sentences.zh: =【贊】=史臣曰：晉卿謹身蒞事，足為純臣，避寇全忠，固彰大節。

translations.literal: = [Eulogy] = The historiographer says: Jinqing guarded himself and attended to affairs—fully a pure minister; avoiding bandits he preserved his integrity, firmly displaying great integrity.
translations.idiomatic: [Eulogy] The historiographer writes: Jinqing conducted himself with care in office and was a true loyal minister; in fleeing the rebels he preserved his integrity and showed great moral courage.

sentences.zh: 然博達精審，豈不知寬猛之道哉！

translations.literal: Yet broadly penetrating and finely examining—how could he not know the way of leniency and severity!
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was learned and discerning—how could he not have known the balance of leniency and severity!

sentences.zh: 奉林甫之旨，順胥吏之意，悅附張倚，欺罔時君。

translations.literal: He followed Linfu's intent, complied with clerks' wishes, pleased and attached to Zhang Yi, and deceived the sovereign of the time.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Li Linfu's wishes, indulged the clerks, curried favor with Zhang Yi, and deceived the emperor.

sentences.zh: 生為重臣，諂林甫之勢也；

translations.literal: In life a great minister—this was fawning on Linfu's power;
translations.idiomatic: In life he was a great minister who flattered Li Linfu's power;

sentences.zh: 歿改美謚，引元載之恩焉。

translations.literal: in death his posthumous name was changed to a fine one—this drew on Yuan Zai's grace.
translations.idiomatic: in death his posthumous name was improved through Yuan Zai's favor.

sentences.zh: 或言晉卿不為巧宦者，誠不信也。

translations.literal: If some say Jinqing was not a crafty official, truly one cannot believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Those who claim Jinqing was no crafty courtier simply cannot be believed.

sentences.zh: 冕力贊中興，名居大位，奉公抱義，可以致身；

translations.literal: Mian vigorously aided the restoration, his name occupied a great position, he embraced the public and held to righteousness—by this one could devote oneself;
translations.idiomatic: Mian vigorously supported the restoration and rose to high office; devoted to public duty and righteousness, he might have been remembered with honor—

sentences.zh: 賣官度僧，是何為政？

translations.literal: yet selling offices and ordaining monks—what sort of government was this?
translations.idiomatic: yet he sold offices and ordained monks—what manner of governance was that?

sentences.zh: 及其老也，貪冒尤深。

translations.literal: When he reached old age, greed and presumption were especially deep.
translations.idiomatic: In old age his greed grew worse still.

sentences.zh: 遵慶學術貞明，為國忠所出；

translations.literal: Zunqing's learning was upright and clear—he was sent out by Guozhong;
translations.idiomatic: Zunqing was learned and upright, though Yang Guozhong posted him to the provinces;

sentences.zh: 恭儉謹密，遇蕭華素知。

translations.literal: respectful, frugal, cautious, and secretive—he met Xiao Hua who had long known him.
translations.idiomatic: respectful, frugal, and discreet—he won recognition from Xiao Hua, who had long known his worth.

sentences.zh: 位重行純，老而彌篤，彼二公固有慚德。

translations.literal: His position was weighty and his conduct pure; in old age he grew more earnest—the other two lords indeed had cause for shame.
translations.idiomatic: He held high rank with pure conduct and grew only more steadfast with age—the other two men had reason to feel shame beside him.

sentences.zh: 向克荷堂構，不墜門風。

translations.literal: Xiang was able to bear the hall's framework and did not let the family's style fall.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang upheld the family legacy and did not let its reputation fall.

sentences.zh: 樞因盜而振，盜憎而亡，宜哉！

translations.literal: Shu rose through the bandit, the bandit hated him and he perished—fitting indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Shu rose through the rebel, and when the rebel turned against him he perished—as was fitting!

sentences.zh: 君子守道遠刑，蓋慮此也。

translations.literal: The gentleman guards the Way and keeps distant from punishment—perhaps he considers this.
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman keeps to the Way and stays clear of punishment—perhaps he had this in mind.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：奧矣晉卿，貪哉裴冕。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: Profound was Jinqing; greedy was Pei Mian.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy reads: Jinqing was profound; Pei Mian was greedy.

sentences.zh: 遵慶父子，及之者鮮。

translations.literal: Zunqing father and sons—few could reach them.
translations.idiomatic: Zunqing and his sons—few could match them.
